observation.visible_scene: A long serpentine arrangement of upright white dominoes laid out in folded parallel rows on a pale marble floor, with a stepped white base at the near-left end holding a single black domino. A person's hand with the index finger extended is at the left edge, poised against the black domino. A 'Taikamuna' watermark sits in the bottom-left corner throughout.
visible_changes: The index finger presses the black domino, which tilts forward and ends up lying flat against the stepped base.
After the black domino falls, the first white dominoes on the stepped base tip and fall in sequence, then the falling wave travels rightward along the bottom straight row.
The hand withdraws and leaves the frame within the first half-second.
The collapse reaches the curved right end and reverses direction, propagating leftward along the middle row.
The middle-row collapse approaches the left curve and begins tipping the top row, which starts falling from left to right as the clip ends.
The standing white dominoes in the not-yet-reached sections remain upright and unchanged, marking the boundary of the traveling collapse.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the top row and the far-right tail eventually fall completely (the segment ends mid-propagation).
Any earlier setup or cause before the finger contact is not shown; the push is the visible onset within this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is minimal but not certain; the marble background and overall layout stay roughly fixed relative to the frame edges, so any drift is small.
Whether the long straight tail on the far right is part of the same continuous chain or a separate line is not fully resolvable from these frames.
